overview.intro:
Chapter 43 covers **raw furskins** — mink, fox, lamb, rabbit, beaver, sable and other pelts (heading 4301) — **tanned or dressed furskins**, including sheepskins with the wool on (4302), **fur garments, accessories and other articles of furskin** (4303) and **artificial fur** (4304). Its **39 tariff lines** carry low base rates: Free on 18 lines, 4% on fur apparel and 6.5% at most, on artificial fur.

Two things decide the cost of an import. First, **whether it may enter at all**: dog and cat fur is banned (19 U.S.C. 1308), seal and other marine-mammal furs are prohibited without an MMPA permit or exception, CITES- and ESA-listed species need permits, wildlife furs need a Fish and Wildlife Service declaration, and fur garments must carry a Fur Products Labeling Act label. Second, **the extra duty by country**: since **July 24, 2026** EU goods pay **10% in total**, and most other suppliers pay a **10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff** on every line. China adds its 2018–2019 Section 301 duties (**41.5%** in total on a fur coat), Brazil 25% more, and **Canada a 50% Section 338 duty** on 11 lines — raw fox, tanned furskins and fur apparel among them — even with a USMCA claim. Italy supplied 27% of the $166M imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Raw furskins: mink, fox, lamb, rabbit, beaver, sable and other pelts
productGroups.blurb: Raw (untanned) pelts: mink, Astrakhan/Persian and similar lamb, fox, and other furskins with statistical lines for hare, rabbit, beaver, muskrat, nutria, lynx, marten, sable, fisher, raccoon and seal, plus heads, tails, paws and pieces. All Free except silver, black or platinum fox (5.1%). Raw sheep and goat skins with the wool or hair on are chapter 41.

productGroups.label: Tanned or dressed furskins, incl. sheepskins with the wool on, pieces and plates
productGroups.blurb: Furskins that have been tanned or dressed, whole or in pieces, loose or sewn into plates and crosses (not yet made into articles): mink 2.1%, named lamb 2.2%, silver fox 5.6%, other fox, beaver, raccoon, sable and similar 1.5% (not dyed) or 2.2% (dyed), rabbit or hare 2.7%, other furskins such as sheepskins 3.5% (not dyed) or 1.7% (dyed), assembled plates 5.3%.

productGroups.label: Fur garments, accessories and other articles of furskin
productGroups.blurb: Fur coats, jackets, vests, stoles, collars and other apparel and clothing accessories of furskin (4303.10, 4%; mink reported separately), including shearling coats, and other articles of furskin such as blankets, throws and rugs (4303.90, Free). Fur hats are chapter 65 and fur-and-leather gloves heading 4203. 74% of the chapter's imports.

productGroups.label: Artificial fur and articles thereof
productGroups.blurb: Artificial fur — fibres gummed or sewn onto leather, woven fabric or other material — and articles of it, 6.5%. workedExamples.title: A $10,000 mink coat: Italy vs China
workedExamples.body: Fur apparel is 4303.10 at 4%. From Italy the EU rule makes the total **10%** (9903.05.39), so the coat pays **$1,000**. The same coat made in China pays 4% + 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) + 12.5% (9903.05.31) = **41.5%, $4,150**. Either way it needs a Fur Products Labeling Act label naming the animal ("Mink") and the country of origin of the fur, and an FWS wildlife declaration (mink is not a domesticated animal under 50 CFR 14.4).

workedExamples.title: Raw mink and fox pelts from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: Ranch-raised Canadian mink (4301.10.00.20) is Free and, with a USMCA claim, exempt from Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93): **$0** on a $50,000 lot. Raw fox other than silver, black or platinum fox (4301.60.60) is on the Section 338 list in U.S. note 51(b)(1) since September 15, 2026, and that 50% (9903.03.12) applies even with USMCA: **$10,000** on $20,000 of pelts. Both need FWS Form 3-177 and a designated or Canadian border port (50 CFR 14.16).

workedExamples.title: Tanned sheepskins from Brazil: undyed vs dyed
workedExamples.body: Other tanned furskins, not dyed (4302.19.60, 3.5%), are on Brazil's exemption list in U.S. note 50(a)(ii) (9903.05.03), so only the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty is added: **16%, $1,600** on $10,000. The same skins dyed (4302.19.75, 1.7%) are not on the list and pay 1.7% + 25% (9903.05.01) + 12.5% (9903.05.27) = **39.2%, $3,920**.

workedExamples.title: A faux fur throw from China: Chapter 43 or not?
workedExamples.body: Only "artificial fur" — fibres gummed or sewn onto a backing — is heading 4304 (6.5%); from China it pays 6.5% + 25% (List 3) + 12.5% = **44%**, $4,400 on $10,000. Imitation fur made by knitting or weaving is excluded by chapter note 5: the fabric is 6001 or 5801, and CBP classed coats of acrylic pile fake fur in chapter 62 (ruling 897570), so the rate follows that chapter instead. Get a ruling before ordering.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Throughout the tariff schedule references to "furskins", other than to raw furskins of heading 4301, apply to hides or skins of all animals which have been tanned or dressed with the hair or wool on.

**Note 2.** This chapter does not cover: (a) birdskins or parts of birdskins, with their feathers or down (heading 0505 or 6701); (b) raw hides or skins, with the hair or wool on, of chapter 41 (see note 1(c) to that chapter); (c) gloves, mittens and mitts consisting of leather and furskin or of leather and artificial fur (heading 4203); (d) articles of chapter 64; (e) headgear or parts thereof of chapter 65; or (f) articles of chapter 95 (for example, toys, games, sports equipment).

**Note 3.** Heading 4303 includes furskins and parts thereof, assembled with the addition of other materials, and furskins and parts thereof, sewn together in the form of garments or parts or accessories of garments or in the form of other articles.

**Note 4.** Articles of apparel and clothing accessories (except those excluded by note 2) lined with furskin or artificial fur or to which furskin or artificial fur is attached on the outside except as mere trimming are to be classified in heading 4303 or 4304 as the case may be.

**Note 5.** Throughout the tariff schedule the expression "artificial fur" means any imitation of furskin consisting of wool, hair or other fibers gummed or sewn on to leather, woven fabric or other materials, but does not include imitation furskins obtained by weaving or knitting (generally, heading 5801 or 6001).

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 39 Chapter 43 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — or 10% in total for EU goods — and no Chapter 43 line is on an exemption list. China keeps its 2018–2019 Section 301 duties, Brazil pays another 25% on 38 of 39 lines, and **Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on 11 lines (fur apparel and fur pieces since August 22, raw fox and tanned furskins since September 15), USMCA claim or not. The $800 de minimis exemption stays suspended, so small fur and faux-fur parcels pay full duty. The import bans on dog and cat fur and marine-mammal furs are unchanged.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 43 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, the Brazil Section 301 tariff and its exemption list, China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Russia column 2 and note 30 rates, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended, and the suspension of de minimis. Standing import bans (dog and cat fur, marine mammals, CITES/ESA species) did not change in this period and are covered under Import documents. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 43 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Two duties. Section 301 (+10%, 9903.05.29) is lifted for USMCA-qualifying goods (9903.05.93). The Section 338 duty of 50% applies even when USMCA is claimed (U.S. note 51(a)) on 11 lines: since August 22, 2026 fur apparel and clothing accessories (4303.10) and raw heads, tails, paws and pieces (4301.90) under note 51(b)(3) (9903.03.14, Proclamation 11048); since September 15, 2026 raw fox other than silver, black or platinum fox (4301.60.60), tanned beaver, fox, raccoon, sable and similar furskins (4302.19.30, 4302.19.45) and other tanned furskins not dyed (4302.19.60) under note 51(b)(1) (9903.03.12, added by Proclamation 11064). Raw mink, raw lamb and other raw whole furskins are not on the list. No Chapter 43 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The 35% IEEPA duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying Canadian raw mink, beaver, sable and other raw pelts pay $0; Canadian fur coats, raw fox and most tanned furskins pay 50% even with USMCA, and 60% or more without it.

inEffect.exemption: Three Section 301 duties reach Chapter 43. List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03, 25% since May 10, 2019) covers all of headings 4302, 4303 and 4304; List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15, since February 14, 2020) covers raw mink (4301.10), raw fox (4301.60) and other raw whole furskins (4301.80.02). understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 43 goods rose from **$146M in 2024 to $166M in 2025** (+13.4%), but stay below the 2022 peak of $214M. Finished goods dominate: **articles of furskin (heading 4303) were $123M, 74%** — fur apparel and accessories $78.5M (+14%) and other articles such as blankets and rugs $44.4M (+29%). Tanned furskins were $21.3M, raw furskins $17.2M (raw mink $14.4M) and artificial fur $4.7M (+32%).

**Italy supplied $44.1M (27%, +38%)**, almost all of it fur apparel and articles, followed by Türkiye ($23.1M, +28%) and France ($10.9M, +24%). **Canada ($19.0M, −11%)** is the raw-fur supplier — $15.4M of its shipments, 89% of all U.S. raw furskin imports, are pelts — and has fallen from $35.0M in 2020. China shrank 29% to $11.7M but still ships almost half of the artificial fur; Brazil ($11.4M) mostly sends tanned furskins; Vietnam tripled to $4.8M.

Through 2025 USMCA-qualifying Canadian pelts paid no extra duty, while most other suppliers paid the IEEPA reciprocal tariff from April 2025. Those duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 EU goods pay 10% in total and most others a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%, and since August–September 2026 Canada's fur apparel, raw fox and tanned furskins pay a 50% Section 338 duty. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on Chapter 43 goods depends far more on **where they come from** than on what they are: base rates run only from Free to 6.5%. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026), and **no Chapter 43 line is exempt** from it. **EU fur pays 10% in total**, Türkiye and Vietnam add 12.5%, **China pays up to 44%** and **Brazil up to 43.1%**. **Canada is the exception**: USMCA raw pelts enter free, but a 50% Section 338 duty on fur apparel, raw fox and tanned furskins applies even to USMCA goods.

seo.shortDescription: The federal rules for each HTS Chapter 43 line — the dog and cat fur ban, the Marine Mammal Protection Act ban on seal fur, CITES and ESA permits, the FWS wildlife declaration and designated ports, Fur Products Labeling Act labels — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, FTAs, Chapter 98 assembly, rulings and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For fur, **whether a shipment may enter matters more than the duty**. Dog and cat fur is banned outright (19 U.S.C. 1308). Seal, sea otter, walrus, polar bear and other marine-mammal furs may not be imported without a Marine Mammal Protection Act permit or exception. Furs of CITES-listed or endangered species — spotted cats, lynx, otters, wolves and others — need CITES documents and, for endangered species, an ESA permit. Every wild-species fur, including ranch mink and fox, needs a Fish and Wildlife Service declaration (Form 3-177) at a designated port; sheep, lamb, European rabbit and other domesticated animals are exempt. Fur garments must carry a Fur Products Labeling Act label naming the animal and the fur's country of origin, and furs must be invoiced the same way.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: claim **USMCA** on Canadian or Mexican furs (it does not lift Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on fur apparel, raw fox and tanned furskins), claim an **FTA or AGOA** rate where the base rate is the cost, use **9802.00.80** for U.S. furskins assembled abroad, get a **binding ruling** where the heading decides the rate (fur vs faux fur vs fur-trimmed textile), and claim **drawback** on re-exports.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on Canadian or Mexican furs
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Canada or Mexico plus the base rate (up to 6.5%)
levers.appliesTo: All 39 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA — e.g. pelts of mink raised in Canada, furskins tanned there, or fur garments made there
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format. Chapter 43 rules: raw furskins must change from another chapter (animals raised or trapped in the territory), tanning (4302) confers origin from any other heading, and making garments or articles (4303–4304) from furskins of any origin qualifies (General Note 11).
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 4301.60.60, 4301.90, 4302.19.30, 4302.19.45, 4302.19.60 and 4303.10 (U.S. note 51(a)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing furskins, fur coats, shearling and faux fur into the U.S. — HS codes, which furs are banned, the labels and declarations required, and the 2026 tariffs by country. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 43 base rates are low — Free on 18 of 39 lines, 4% on fur apparel, 6.5% at most — and unchanged since January 2025. The extra duty by country and the entry rules decide the cost.

Dog and cat fur is banned (19 U.S.C. 1308), seal and other marine-mammal furs need an MMPA permit or exception, and CITES- or ESA-listed species need permits. Wild-species furs, including ranch mink and fox, need FWS Form 3-177; fur garments need a Fur Products Labeling Act label.
Since July 24, 2026 EU fur pays 10% in total and most other suppliers 10% or 12.5% more under Section 301; no Chapter 43 line is exempt.

China pays up to 44% in total (List 3 + 12.5%), Brazil up to 43.1% (undyed tanned furskins exempt from its 25%), and Canada 50% under Section 338 on fur apparel, raw fox and tanned furskins even with USMCA. USMCA raw mink still enters free.
The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026; the $800 de minimis exemption stays suspended.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 43 cover?
faqs.answer: Furskins and artificial fur. Heading 4301 is raw furskins (mink, lamb, fox, rabbit, beaver, sable, seal and other pelts, plus pieces), 4302 tanned or dressed furskins — including sheepskins with the wool on — not yet made into articles, 4303 fur apparel, accessories and other articles of furskin, and 4304 artificial fur. The 39 lines are Free to 6.5%. Raw sheep skins with the wool on are chapter 41, fur hats chapter 65 and fur-and-leather gloves heading 4203.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and duty for a fur coat?
faqs.answer: Fur coats, jackets, vests, stoles and other apparel and clothing accessories of furskin are 4303.10.00 — .30 for mink, .60 for other fur — at a 4% general rate. The total depends on origin: 10% from the EU, 16.5% from Türkiye or Vietnam, 41.5% from China, 41.5% from Brazil, and 50% from Canada even with a USMCA claim. A textile coat with only fur trim stays in chapters 61–62.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for faux fur?
faqs.answer: Only "artificial fur" — wool, hair or other fibres gummed or sewn onto leather, fabric or another backing — and articles of it are 4304.00.00 (6.5%). Faux fur made by knitting or weaving is excluded by chapter note 5: the fabric is 6001 (knitted pile) or 5801 (woven pile), and garments of it are classified in chapters 61 and 62 (CBP ruling 897570 put acrylic-pile fake fur coats in 6202). From China, 4304 goods pay 44% in total.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for shearling and sheepskin coats and rugs?
faqs.answer: Sheepskin tanned with the wool on is a furskin (chapter note 1). A shearling coat is 4303.10.00.60 at 4% (CBP ruling N277695); tanned sheepskins not yet made up are 4302.19 (3.5% undyed, 1.7% dyed; Persian, Caracul and similar lamb 2.2%), and rugs and other articles of furskin are 4303.90.00, Free. Raw sheepskins with the wool on are chapter 41. Sheep are a domesticated species, so no FWS declaration is needed.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a fur blanket or throw?
faqs.answer: Blankets, throws, rugs and other articles made of real furskin are 4303.90.00, Free at the general rate (from China 37.5%, from the EU 10%). Faux fur throws made of knitted or woven pile fabric are not chapter 43; they are textile blankets or throws — CBP classified a faux fur blanket in 6301.40 (8.5%, ruling N343153). Only articles of artificial fur — fibres gummed or sewn onto a backing — are 4304.

faqs.question: Is it legal to import fur into the U.S.?
searchedAs: is fur legal in the us
is mink fur legal in the us
is fox fur legal in us
are fur coats illegal in the us
faqs.answer: Yes for most furs, such as mink, fox, rabbit, sable or sheepskin, under federal law — but dog and cat fur is banned (19 U.S.C. 1308), seal and other marine-mammal furs need an MMPA permit or exception, and CITES- or ESA-listed species need permits. Wild-species furs, including ranch mink and fox, need FWS Form 3-177 at a designated port, and fur garments need a Fur Products Labeling Act label. Some states restrict retail fur sales; this page covers federal rules.

faqs.question: Is seal fur legal in the U.S.?
searchedAs: is seal fur legal in the us
is seal skin legal in the us
is seal fur illegal in us
faqs.answer: Importing seal fur or sealskin is prohibited. The Marine Mammal Protection Act makes it unlawful to import any marine mammal or marine-mammal product — the FWS definition expressly includes raw, dressed or dyed fur or skin — except under an MMPA permit or exception (50 CFR 216.12, 18.12). The schedule still has a statistical line for raw seal furskins (4301.80.02.80), but that does not make imports lawful.

faqs.question: Is dog and cat fur banned in the U.S.?
searchedAs: dog and cat protection act of 2000
dog and cat fur protection act
faqs.answer: Yes. The Dog and Cat Protection Act of 2000 (19 U.S.C. 1308) bans importing, exporting, making or selling any product made wholly or partly of dog fur (Canis familiaris) or cat fur (Felis catus). Penalties run up to $10,000 per knowing violation, the goods are forfeited and repeat violators can be barred from the fur trade. The only exception is a deceased personal pet. The ban also covers goods sold as faux fur.

faqs.question: What does the Fur Products Labeling Act require?
faqs.answer: Every fur garment must carry a label giving the animal name from the FTC's Fur Products Name Guide, the country of origin of the fur, and whether the fur is dyed or otherwise colored, used, or made of paws, tails, bellies or waste fur, plus the maker's or seller's name or RN (15 U.S.C. 69b; 16 CFR part 301). Since the Truth in Fur Labeling Act the old small-value exemption is gone. CBP requires the same data on invoices and can order relabeling at entry (19 CFR 11.12a, 141.89).

faqs.question: Do fur imports need an FWS Form 3-177 or CITES permit?
faqs.answer: Most do. FWS treats any wild species as wildlife even when ranch-raised, so mink, fox, sable, raccoon and other furs need a Form 3-177 declaration and clearance at a designated port (or a border port for Canadian-origin wildlife); commercial importers also need an FWS license and pay inspection fees. Lamb, sheep and European rabbit are domesticated and exempt. CITES documents are needed only for listed species such as lynx, otters, wolves and spotted cats.

faqs.question: Can you travel to the U.S. with a fur coat?
searchedAs: can you travel with fur coats
faqs.answer: Yes. Wildlife products worn as clothing or carried in personal baggage and not intended for sale need no FWS declaration (50 CFR 14.62(b)(2)) — unless the species needs a CITES or ESA permit, and raw or dressed furs, as opposed to finished garments, still require Form 3-177. The bans still apply: a coat of seal, dog or cat fur, or of an ESA-endangered species, cannot be brought in.

faqs.question: What tariff applies to fur coats from China?
faqs.answer: 41.5% on a fur coat: the 4% base rate, 25% under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) and 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31). Artificial fur goods pay 44%, tanned furskins 39%–43.1%, and most raw mink or fox pelts 20%. No exclusion covers Chapter 43, and USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the List 3 and 4A duties continue. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What duty do Italian fur and shearling coats pay?
faqs.answer: 10% of value in total. Since July 24, 2026 EU goods whose base rate is under 10% pay 10% in place of the base rate (9903.05.39), and every Chapter 43 rate is under 10% — so a 4% Italian mink or shearling coat pays 10%, and even Free raw pelts pay 10%. Before that, EU goods paid 15% under IEEPA until February 24, 2026, then the 10% Section 122 surcharge to July 23. Italy supplied $44.1M, 27% of 2025 imports.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on fur from Canada?
faqs.answer: USMCA-qualifying raw mink, beaver, sable and other raw pelts enter free. But a 50% Section 338 duty applies even with USMCA to Canadian fur apparel and raw fur pieces (since August 22, 2026) and to raw fox other than silver, black or platinum fox and tanned furskins (since September 15, 2026). Without a USMCA claim, 10% Section 301 is added. Canada supplied $15.4M of the $17.2M of raw furskins imported in 2025.

faqs.question: How much fur does the U.S. import?
faqs.answer: $166M in 2025, up 13.4% from $146M in 2024 but below the 2022 peak of $214M. Articles of furskin were 74% ($123M: apparel $78.5M, other articles $44.4M), tanned furskins $21.3M, raw furskins $17.2M and artificial fur $4.7M. Italy supplied 27%, Türkiye 14%, Canada 11% and China 7%.
